label: Total Crossings (Jul 30 - Aug 4)
source: House of Commons Library / CNN / Ceuta city government
contestNote: Spanish Interior Ministry initially said 49,000-50,000 in 24 hours; Mayor Vivas said 60,000; cumulative full-crisis estimates range up to 80,000.

label: Confirmed Deaths
contestNote: Rose from an initial 72 (Aug 2) to 86 (Sky News) to 111 (100 in Ceuta, 11 in Fnideq) by Aug 4; some later-recovered bodies not definitively linked to the crisis. NGO Caminando Fronteras separately tallies 141 (Aug 5), a figure Spanish officials confirmed to media without formally adopting as the state count.

label: Migrants Still in Ceuta
contestNote: As of Aug 20, most were living unsheltered at the El Trampolín beach camp rather than in official facilities; police began clearing the camp that day.

label: Beach Camp Migrants Relocated to Shelters
contestNote: Transferred to two new temporary reception centres, Loma Margarita and El Embolsamiento (1,800 combined initial capacity), as police cleared the El Trampolín beach camp; roughly 500 people reported to have returned to the beach afterward.

label: Unaccompanied Minors Identified
contestNote: Includes ~500 girls Spain is preparing to transfer to specialised mainland facilities without transferring legal guardianship to receiving regions, over EU preference for repatriation to Morocco and refusal by several autonomous communities to accept minors.

label: CETI Reception Centre Occupancy
contestNote: Unaccompanied-minors facility separately reported at 2,400% of ordinary capacity per Mayor Vivas.

label: EU States Imposing Border Checks on Spain
contestNote: Italy, France, Finland, Austria, Sweden, Denmark and Czechia had each reimposed or announced border controls linked to the crisis.

label: Italy-Spain Schengen Suspension Runs Until
contestNote: Two separate, reciprocal measures: Italy notified the European Commission its checks on Spanish arrivals run until September 1 (could be lifted or extended); Spain's checks on Italian arrivals, imposed Aug 8 after Rome rejected Madrid's ultimatum, run until at least September 7.

label: Ceuta Business Losses (as of Aug 11)
contestNote: Includes an estimated €10.2M from the cancelled patron-saint festivities alone, plus ~90% August tourism booking cancellations.
